description:
The National Agriculture Market (e-NAM) is an initiative launched by the Government of India on April 14, 2016. 

This scheme aims to create a unified national market for agricultural commodities. 

The primary objective of e-NAM is to enhance farmers' income by providing them with better price discovery and reducing the role of intermediaries. 

The initiative seeks to integrate 585 regulated wholesale markets across the country into a single online platform. 

The government aims to facilitate the sale of agricultural produce directly from farmers to buyers through this platform. 

The e-NAM platform allows farmers to sell their produce at competitive prices. 

Farmers can access real-time information on prices and market trends through the e-NAM portal. 

The scheme also aims to promote transparency in the agricultural market. 

Farmers can register on the e-NAM platform free of cost. 

The registration process requires farmers to provide basic details such as their name, address, and bank account information. 

Farmers must also provide proof of land ownership or lease agreements. 

The e-NAM platform supports various commodities including fruits, vegetables, grains, and pulses. 

As of October 2023, over 1.7 crore farmers have registered on the e-NAM platform. 

The platform has facilitated transactions worth over ₹1.5 lakh crore since its inception. 

e-NAM operates on a digital platform that connects farmers with buyers across the country. 

The scheme aims to eliminate the barriers of state borders in agricultural marketing. 

Farmers can sell their produce to buyers from different states without any restrictions. 

The e-NAM platform is designed to provide farmers with access to multiple markets. 

Farmers can choose to sell their produce in the market that offers the best price. 

The platform also provides a mechanism for quality assurance. 

Farmers can get their produce tested for quality before selling it on the platform. 

The e-NAM scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) plays a crucial role in promoting e-NAM. 

State Agricultural Marketing Boards are responsible for the implementation of e-NAM at the state level. 

The government has allocated ₹2,000 crore for the implementation of e-NAM. 

The scheme is part of the larger Digital India initiative. 

e-NAM aims to leverage technology to improve the agricultural sector. 

Farmers can access the e-NAM platform through mobile apps and websites. 

The platform is available in multiple languages to cater to farmers across different regions. 

The government has also launched a helpline number for farmers to assist them with the registration process. 

The helpline number is available in multiple languages to ensure accessibility. 

The e-NAM platform has been integrated with various state agricultural marketing portals. 

This integration allows for seamless transactions across different states. 

Farmers can also avail themselves of various government schemes through the e-NAM platform. 

The scheme encourages farmers to adopt modern farming practices. 

It also promotes the use of technology in agriculture. 

The government aims to increase the number of registered farmers on the e-NAM platform to 2 crore by 2025. 

The e-NAM platform has also been instrumental in promoting organic farming. 

Farmers can sell organic produce at premium prices through the platform. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from farmers across the country. 

Many farmers have reported increased income due to better price realization. 

The government is continuously working to enhance the features of the e-NAM platform. 

New functionalities are being added to improve user experience. 

The e-NAM scheme has also been linked with the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) scheme. 

This linkage ensures that farmers receive direct financial assistance along with better market access. 

The government is also working on integrating e-NAM with the National Food Security Mission. 

This integration aims to ensure food security while enhancing farmers' income. 

The e-NAM platform is expected to play a crucial role in achieving the goal of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

The government has set a target of increasing the share of agriculture in the GDP to 25% by 2025. 

The e-NAM scheme is a significant step towards achieving these targets. 

The platform has also facilitated the export of agricultural commodities. 

Farmers can connect with international buyers through the e-NAM platform. 

The government is promoting e-NAM as a model for other countries to follow. 

The scheme has been recognized globally for its innovative approach to agricultural marketing. 

The e-NAM platform has received several awards for its contribution to the agricultural sector. 

The government is committed to expanding the reach of e-NAM to more farmers. 

Efforts are being made to include more agricultural commodities on the platform. 

The e-NAM initiative is a game-changer for the agricultural sector in India. 

It empowers farmers by providing them with the tools and resources needed for better market access. 

The scheme is expected to transform the agricultural landscape in India. 

The government continues to monitor and evaluate the progress of e-NAM regularly. 

Feedback from farmers is taken into consideration for further improvements. 

The e-NAM platform is a testament to the government's commitment to improving the lives of farmers. 

The initiative is aligned with the broader goals of rural development and poverty alleviation. 

The e-NAM scheme is a significant milestone in the journey towards a more robust agricultural economy in India.
